div.l: But with thees Reliques whan̄ that he fonde
A pore parsoıı̄un duelling vpon lond .
Vpon oo·day he gat him more money
Then that ꝑpersoıı̄un gat in monthis twey
And thus with feyned flatery and iapes
He made the parsoıı̄un and the peple his Apes
But truly to telle at the laste
He was in church a noble eccliāste
Wel couth he rede a lessoıı̄un ⁊and a Storie ·
But aldirbest he sang an Offertorie
For wel he wist when that song was sunge
Him must preche and wel affile his tunge
To wynne Siluer as he wel coude
Therfore he sang the merierly ⁊and loude
¶ Nowe haue I told you sothely in a clause
Thestate tharray the nombre ⁊and eke the cause
Why that assemblid was this cumpany
In Southwerk at this gentil hostery
That hight the Tabard fast by the belle
But now is time to you forto telle
Hough that we bare us that ilke night̄
When that we were in that hostry alight̄
And aftir wille I telle of oure viage
And alle the remaynant of oure pilgⁱrimage
But first I pray you of your curtesy
That ye narret it not my vilany
Though that I plainly speke in this matier͗e
To telle you her wurdis and her chere
Ne thoug I ne speke her wurdis ꝓpropirly
For this ye knowen̄ also wele as I ·
Whoso shal telle a tale aftir a man̄
He mut reherce as nygh as euer he can̄
Euery wurd if it be in his charge
All speke he neuer so rudely and large
Or ellis he must telle his tale vntrue
Or feyne thing or finde wurdis newe
He may not spare al though he wer̉e his broþ̉er
He must as wel sey one wurd as anoþ̉er
Crist spac himselue ful brode in holy writte
And wel ye wote no vilanye is it
